results.title: OpenClaw Architecture Explained
results.snippet: Most directly on-target for the isolation/routing angle. Describes a centralized Gateway control plane that handles routing, access control, session management, and orchestration but does NOT execute agent logic. Sessions are 'isolated conversation contexts' — each keeps its own state, message history, and workspace on disk, so agents do NOT share state across sessions. Key rule: 'one active run per session' (additional requests queue until the current run finishes) to prevent race conditions / keep state deterministic; multiple agents run in parallel each in its own session. Session state persists to disk as JSON (moves to S3 in serverless so stateless Lambdas rebuild context per invocation); a session holds message history, workspace metadata (cwd, open files, env vars), agent config (model, temp, tools), and execution context (pending tasks, scheduled actions, webhooks). Runtime is a 6-phase turn loop (context assembly → model invocation → response processing → tool execution → state update → response delivery), tools run sequentially within the session's permission boundaries. Sandboxing options: Docker container per runtime with mounted workspace volumes, VMs, or restricted unprivileged user contexts. Caveat: marketing blog, names only SOUL.md, serverless-openclaw, and ClawHub — no internal module paths.

results.title: OpenClaw Architecture, Explained (ppaolo)
results.snippet: Single richest HOW-it-works source for my angle. Live Canvas (A2UI): runs as a separate server process (default port 18793) for isolation; agent calls a canvas update method, server parses `a2ui-component`/`a2ui-action` HTML attributes and pushes over WebSocket; button clicks return to the agent as tool calls (declarative HTML, no JS) — a reusable state-externalization pattern. Talk Mode/Voice Wake: always-on wake-word ('Hey OpenClaw') or push-to-talk; audio to ElevenLabs for STT/TTS; Talk Mode adds continuous hands-free dialogue with interruption detection. Persona is layered prompt composition: `AGENTS.md` (non-negotiable global rules) + optional `SOUL.md` (personality/tone) + `TOOLS.md`, plus dynamic session history/skills/memory-search. Self-state externalized to files: sessions in `~/.openclaw/sessions/` as append-only event log w/ branching; memory in `~/.openclaw/memory/<agentId>.sqlite` (vector + BM25 hybrid search); `MEMORY.md` + `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. Memory-flush promotes durable info before compaction (skipped when workspace not writable). Onboarding via `openclaw onboard` CLI. Selective skill injection (`skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`, only relevant skill injected to avoid prompt bloat). Maps to Rivet's affordance/cognitive-mirror externalization and prefix-cache concerns. Caveat: third-party code reading, not official docs.

results.title: OpenClaw and the Programmable Soul (duncsand)
results.snippet: Best dedicated source on self-state/identity-continuity (sub-question 5). Four primitives: persistent identity across sessions, periodic autonomy via a 'heartbeat' (agent acts unprompted, no audit trail/approval between beats), accumulated memory files, and social context (Moltbook). Identity lives in a writable local `SOUL.md` markdown the user owns, defining 'who the agent is, how it should behave, what it values.' On every wake cycle the agent reads SOUL.md first — it 'reads itself into being,' likened to glancing in a mirror (directly analogous to Rivet's cognitive-mirror/self-state injection). Identity is mutable at the file level: anything that can modify SOUL.md changes who the agent is (a 'conversion' install script rewrites SOUL.md). Frozen/oracle state: when an owner leaves, SOUL.md is marked 'frozen in time' and the agent goes read-only — an identity-continuity-after-departure pattern.

results.title: [OpenClaw] 8 Ways to Stop Agents from Losing Context
results.snippet: The single most directly portable source for Rivet. Documents 8 concrete techniques with file paths against openclaw/openclaw tag v2026.2.1. CRITICAL for Rivet's DeepSeek prefix-cache focus: Technique 5 'cache-aware pruning / prefix caching' (extension.ts, pruner.ts) tracks server-side prompt-prefix cache timing locally, keeps the prefix stable while cache is valid, and prunes ONLY when it expires; two-phase trim at >30% (soft head+tail shrink) and >50% (hard placeholder), last 3 assistant turns always protected. Also: pre-turn memory flush gated by shouldFlushMemory / memoryFlushCompactionCount writing facts to MEMORY.md (agent-runner.ts, memory-flush.ts); context-window guards (16K hard floor FailoverError, 32K warning); turn-based history limiting; head/tail preservation (4000-char results trimmed to first 1500 + last 1500); adaptive chunk ratio 0.15-0.4; staged summarization.

results.title: OpenClaw Session Management Deep Dive (Compaction reference)
results.snippet: Most authoritative data-structure-level source. Two persistence layers: sessions.json (key/value sessionKey->SessionEntry, mutable) and per-session <sessionId>.jsonl append-only transcript with tree structure (id + parentId). Paths: ~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/sessions/. SessionEntry tracks inputTokens/outputTokens/totalTokens/contextTokens/compactionCount/memoryFlushAt. Compaction is run by the Pi runtime (@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent SessionManager), triggered on overflow OR when contextTokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens; writes a persistent 'compaction' summary entry with firstKeptEntryId + tokensBefore. Config: reserveTokens 16384, keepRecentTokens 20000, enforced floor 20000 via ensurePiCompactionReserveTokens(). Memory flush is a silent NO_REPLY agentic turn at softThresholdTokens below Pi threshold, once per cycle, writes memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md. NOTE: this doc explicitly does NOT mention prefix/prompt caching.

results.title: Agent Control Loops: From OpenClaw to Alternative Architectures
results.snippet: Most directly on-angle for the main loop. Describes OpenClaw as a single-model agentic loop wrapped around the Pi agent core (@mariozechner/pi-agent-core) via RPC. The long-lived Gateway (Node.js, ws://127.0.0.1:18789) runs a fixed per-turn pipeline: intake -> assign to a serial per-session lane queue (prevents shared-state races) -> context assembly -> model inference -> tool execution -> stream reply -> persist state, looping until final response or 600s timeout. State is three file-based systems making it survive restarts: JSONL transcripts (audit log), MEMORY.md (curated, read+written each turn), SOUL.md (personality, model-mutable). Each turn the prompt is rebuilt from user msg + tool schemas + session history + MEMORY.md + SOUL.md; tool results append back; auto-compaction summarizes/prunes near the window limit. Caveat: stopping is implicit (same model judges completion, no external verifier).

results.title: OpenClaw Architecture, Explained (ppaolo Substack)
results.snippet: Gives concrete source paths and the cross-session persistence data structure. Gateway = WebSocket server at src/gateway/server.ts (Node 22+, 127.0.0.1:18789), 'single source of truth.' Agent runtime in src/agents/piembeddedrunner.ts using Pi Agent Core with RPC + streaming; per turn it resolves session, assembles context, streams while executing tools, persists state. Key for the angle: each conversation is stored as a session file under ~/.openclaw/sessions/ as an APPEND-ONLY EVENT LOG with branching support, enabling restart recovery. Session IDs double as security boundaries (agent:<id>:main vs DM/group, sandboxed by default). Memory at ~/.openclaw/memory/<agentId>.sqlite (vector + BM25 hybrid); file watcher reindexes with 1.5s debounce. Context assembled per turn from persisted JSON history + dynamic system prompt from workspace files + semantic-search memory pull, not an ever-growing transcript.

results.title: openclaw/docs/concepts/memory.md (official docs, GitHub)
results.snippet: Authoritative anchor for state/memory persistence. Core principle: 'The model only remembers what gets saved to disk - there is no hidden state.' Plain Markdown in workspace (default ~/.openclaw/workspace): MEMORY.md (durable, loaded into bootstrap prompt every DM session), memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md daily notes (today+yesterday auto-loaded; indexed for memory_search/memory_get but NOT injected each turn), optional DREAMS.md. Default backend SQLite (keyword+vector+hybrid). If MEMORY.md exceeds budget, on-disk file is intact but injected copy is truncated (inspect via /context list, /context detail, openclaw doctor). Continuous-state safeguards: automatic memory flush (silent turn before compaction to save context), opt-in Dreaming (scores short-term signals in memory/.dreams/, threshold-promotes to MEMORY.md), grounded backfill (rem-backfill --stage-short-term, deep-promotion-only writes), and short-lived Commitments delivered via heartbeat. Mechanism is file persistence + SQLite index, not a single in-memory snapshot object.

results.title: How OpenClaw's Memory System Actually Works (Shivam Agarwal, Medium)
results.snippet: Deepest implementation detail on the SQLite backing store and flush mechanism, useful for porting to Rivet. Two-tier file memory in workspace: daily logs memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md (append-only ephemeral), MEMORY.md (curated, loads only in private sessions, never group), session transcripts sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md (searchable when experimental.sessionMemory:true). Injection: session start loads today+yesterday logs; older context via hybrid search. SQLite at ~/.openclaw/memory/{agentId}.sqlite with tables files, chunks, embedding_cache (SHA-256 dedup), chunks_fts (FTS5), vec_chunks (sqlite-vec, JS cosine fallback); ~400-token chunks w/ 80-token overlap; retrieval fusion 70% vector / 30% BM25 by union. State snapshot = pre-compaction flush: at contextWindow - reserveTokensFloor - softThresholdTokens (~176K of 200K) a silent agentic turn writes durable memory; tracks memoryFlushCompactionCount to avoid double-flush, replies NO_REPLY when nothing to save. Caveat: single-author, verify keys against official docs.

results.title: Agent Control Loops: From OpenClaw to Alternative Architectures
results.snippet: Best source on the runtime kernel and process model. Gateway = long-lived Node.js process on host, listens ws://127.0.0.1:18789. results.title: How to Build and Secure a Personal AI Agent with OpenClaw
results.snippet: Strongest anchor for sandbox/permission model (Q2) and session isolation (Q3). Three-layer arch (Channel/Brain/Body) on one Gateway running as systemd/LaunchAgent, loopback bind. Seven-stage loop: channel normalization (Baileys/grammY adapters) -> command-queue session serialization (one-at-a-time, prevents state corruption) -> context assembly (base prompt + COMPACT skills list of names/desc/paths only) -> inference with 'compaction reserve' buffer -> ReAct -> on-demand full SKILL.md load -> Markdown persistence in ~/.openclaw/workspace/ + sqlite-vec embedding search. Sandbox: tool allowlist/denylist, DENIES 'gateway' tool so agent can't edit own config, filesystem MCP scoped to one folder, separate browser defaultProfile. Access control: dmPolicy allowlist + allowFrom, groupPolicy disabled / requireMention, mandatory gateway token, chmod 700/600 on workspace. Indirect prompt-injection defense lives in AGENTS.md.

results.title: Transcript: OpenClaw — Peter Steinberger (Lex Fridman)
results.snippet: Author's own design rationale — the practitioner angle's primary anchor, strongest for Q5 (self-state/identity). Steinberger deliberately made the agent self-aware of its own makeup: it 'knows what his source code is', 'understands how it sits and runs in its own harness', knows which model it runs and where docs are. This enabled self-modification ('the agent would just modify its own software'). Identity via SOUL: he told it how to interact then 'write your own agents.md give yourself a name'; keeps SOUL private as a canary. Loop iterated 'like a game' — added a no-reply token so it can 'shut up' in group chats; worked on message queuing. Memory = 'level two or three with Markdown files and the vector database', RL as the imagined endgame. Notes agents 'always start fresh' and that models 'freak out' near context limit.

results.snippet: Most concrete source on the SKILL definition/loading/routing model. Skills are SKILL.md files (instructions + metadata) that can run shell commands and call APIs. Loading uses a 3-tier resolution priority: workspace ./skills (highest, per-agent) > managed ~/.openclaw/skills (shared across agents) > bundled (ships with OpenClaw, lowest). Config in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json under skills.entries.<name> with enabled flag, env injection (only if not already set), and apiKey for skills declaring primaryEnv. Metadata fields named: requires.bins, install commands. Key portable caveat: 'API keys are injected into the HOST process during agent runs, not the sandbox' — secrets are exposed to the agent. clawhub info/list/install CLI manages registry retrieval.

results.title: How to Set Up OpenClaw Sandbox for Secure Agent Isolation (Fastio)
results.snippet: Best detail on the host-vs-isolated execution boundary. Sandbox sits between the Gateway (always stays on host, never moves) and the filesystem/process tools: exec, read, write, edit, apply_patch, process. Three config axes: mode (off / non-main / all), container scope (agent=1 per agent default / session / shared), workspaceAccess (none=isolated dir default / ro mounted at /agent which disables write+edit+apply_patch / rw mounted at /workspace). Docker backend default, fails fast if image missing (no auto-pull). Network defaults to none (blocks exfiltration); host networking and namespace joining blocked. Bind-mount blocklist: /var/run/docker.sock, /etc /proc /sys /dev, ~/.aws ~/.ssh ~/.gnupg ~/.docker ~/.config ~/.cargo ~/.netrc ~/.npm — validation resolves symlinks through deepest existing ancestor and fails closed even when leaf path doesn't exist.

results.title: Sandbox OpenClaw Shell Commands in 12 Minutes (Markaicode)
results.snippet: Directly covers tool routing/permission policy and the trust model behind session isolation. Default: main session (1:1 chat) runs exec on the HOST with full user privileges by design ('YOU talking to YOUR assistant'); non-main sessions (groups, Discord, Slack, channels) get ephemeral Docker containers. Tool policy uses allowlisting over denylisting: tools.exec.safeBins (e.g. ls/cat/grep), and tools.policy.allow/deny lists gating tool names (bash, read, write, sessions_list, sessions_send vs browser, canvas, cron). Names concrete attack vectors: prompt injection, malicious SKILL.md snippets, gateway-token exfiltration (CVE-2026-25253), weaker models more susceptible to instruction hijacking.

results.title: How to Fix OpenClaw Shell Command Execution — exec disabled by default (Markaicode)
results.snippet: Useful falsifiable fact on the default permission posture: OpenClaw's exec tool is OFF by default since January 2026; enabling requires adding a tool 'profile' (e.g. "profile": "coding") to the tools config then restarting the gateway. Documents granular per-tool enablement, reinforcing that capability grants are explicit/opt-in rather than default-on.

results.title: OpenClaw: architecture and hardening guide (Nebius)
results.snippet: Architecture overview naming the four core subsystems relevant to state + capability extension: Nodes (execute agent workloads), Sessions (maintain conversational state), Tools and skills (extend agent capabilities), Memory (stores context across interactions). Frames how skills sit alongside the Gateway/session/memory layers; useful for mapping the overall component model rather than line-level skill mechanics.

results.title: OpenClaw in 2026: Architecture, Setup, Skills Security, and a Hardened Enterprise Checklist (50Pros)
results.snippet: Background + skills-security framing: confirms lineage (Clawdbot → Moltbot → OpenClaw), MIT license, author Peter Steinberger (ex-PSPDFKit). Provides a skills-security hardening checklist that complements the sandbox/permission mechanics, treating community skills as untrusted code requiring audit before enabling. Lighter on source-level implementation than the Markaicode/Fastio guides.
